Derive the figures a filing left out

Source: R/xbrl_fill.R
xbrl_fill.Rd

A filer may report the components of a subtotal without the subtotal, or the subtotal without one of its components. Both are ordinary, and both leave a statistic short of a variable it needs. The presentation hierarchy names every line that belongs, so both can be recovered.

Usage

xbrl_fill(
  x,
  taxonomy = NULL,
  statement = c("BalanceSheetAccountForm", "BalanceSheetReportForm"),
  residual = "default",
  by = c("basis", "period"),
  tol = 1
)

Arguments

x

A tibble from add_taxonomy().

taxonomy

A cvrr_taxonomy from read_taxonomy(), or a list of them. The hierarchy is what names the missing line; the reported facts alone cannot say which line is absent.

statement

Restrict to these statements. Defaults to the balance sheet, for the reason above.

residual

Which line receives a remainder that cannot be attributed to one absent component: a named character vector, subtotal to line. "default" (the default) uses the map for the Danish balance sheet described below; NULL derives only where exactly one component is missing.

by

Columns identifying one statement. Default c("basis", "period").

tol

Absolute tolerance in the reporting currency. Default 1.

Value

x with derived rows appended and a source column added: "reported", "derived: sum of components", "derived: residual" (one component was missing, so the remainder is that component) or "derived: remainder to residual line" (several were missing, and the remainder went to the line whose purpose is to hold it).

What is derived, and what is not

Two cases, and only these two.

A subtotal is derived where the taxonomy places one over lines the filing reports and the subtotal itself is untagged. Its value is the sum of the nearest reported lines beneath it.

A component is derived where the subtotal is reported, its reported components fall short, and the taxonomy leaves exactly one line unaccounted for. The residual is that line. This is how Anden gæld comes back: filers routinely give the specified debts and the total and leave the remainder unnamed.

Where two or more lines are missing, arithmetic cannot say which of them the remainder belongs to. But a statement has a line whose purpose is to hold what is left over – Anden gæld, Andre tilgodehavender – and where that line is among the missing ones, the remainder belongs there by definition rather than by guess. residual names those lines; see below.

Why the residual line has to be named

There is no structural way to find it. LongtermLiabilitiesOtherThanProvisions has 37 children in the 2023 taxonomy, three of whose Danish labels begin "Anden" or "Andre": provisions, bond debt, and the catch-all. Only the third is a remainder line; the other two are named categories that happen to start with the same word. Element names carry the same trap – 67 elements begin Other, and most are ordinary categories.

Nor does presentation order help: the catch-all sits 28th of the 37, not last. So the map is written out by hand from the labels, it covers the Danish balance sheet, and a caller with a different statement supplies their own. A rule that guessed would put bond debt where trade creditors belong.

Signs, and why only the balance sheet

This works on lines that add up without a sign convention – assets, liabilities, equity. The income statement is not filled: its lines carry signs the filer chose, so a residual there is not a value but a value and a direction, and check_cascade() is the tool that resolves those.

A derived figure is not a reported one

Every row comes back with source, and the derived ones say how they were arrived at. A statistic that cannot distinguish the two will eventually publish an inference as an observation, so the column is not optional and the derived rows are not silently merged.

See also

check_statement(), which reports the same two situations without resolving them, and check_movement(), whose assume_nil is the same idea applied to a schedule's endpoints.

Other taxonomy: add_taxonomy(), check_breakdown(), check_cascade(), check_continuity(), check_inclusion(), check_movement(), check_statement(), read_taxonomy(), xbrl_accounts(), xbrl_company(), xbrl_lines(), xbrl_movements(), xbrl_note_tables(), xbrl_period(), xbrl_resolve()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# one filing, so the default grouping is the whole of it
x <- read_xbrl("13645183_2024-12-31.xml")
filled <- xbrl_fill(x)

filled[filled$source != "reported", c("elementid", "label", "value", "source")]

# a directory: the grouping has to say which filing a line belongs to
xbrl_fill(read_xbrl("materiale/xbrl"), by = c("file", "basis", "period"))
} # }
